**/

import * as runtime from './runtime/library.js';
import $Types = runtime.Types // general types
import $Public = runtime.Types.Public
import $Utils = runtime.Types.Utils
import $Extensions = runtime.Types.Extensions
import $Result = runtime.Types.Result

export type PrismaPromise<T> = $Public.PrismaPromise<T>


/**
 * Model discussionboard_channels
 * Channel Master - Implements the forum partition and board organization from 'Discussion Board Management'. Provides structural root for categorizing boards into high-level channels like 'Politics', 'Economics', etc. Enforces 3NF by avoiding redundancy in boards/posts and enabling scalable navigation.
 * 
 * @namespace Systematic
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussionboard_channels = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_channelsPayload>
/**
 * Model discussionboard_sections
 * Section Master - Implements channel subdivision for structured forum hierarchy (Channel → Section → Board). Reduces clutter; 3NF prevents board/post denormalization. Maps to forum topics (Asia, Policy, Announcements, etc). Enforces single-channel constraint—each section must belong to a channel.
 * 
 * @namespace Systematic
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussionboard_sections = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_sectionsPayload>
/**
 * Model discussionboard_configurations
 * System Configuration Store - Implements global/system-level settings and toggles for runtime business flexibility. 3NF, one config per row (no lists/blobs). Used for feature flags, thresholds, and system parameters per requirements. No denormalized summaries; config items managed independently.
 * 
 * @namespace Systematic
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussionboard_configurations = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_configurationsPayload>
/**
 * Model discussionboard_notifications
 * System Notification Log - Logs every system notification sent for delivery record, debugging, and compliance ('Notifications & Updates', 'Audit & Compliance'). Information is normalized—does not calculate or store aggregate counts. Optionally associates with a user/entity by uuid, never with denormalized info. Does not duplicate status info already elsewhere (only atomic notification row).
 * 
 * @namespace Systematic
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussionboard_notifications = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_notificationsPayload>
/**
 * Model discussionboard_settings
 * Per-Feature/Area Settings Table - Stores specific settings applicable to a context/scope (not global configs). Used for per-channel/section/feature toggles as per 'System Settings' requirements. 3NF, does not duplicate values from configuration. Scoped by id/type (nullable when not tied to a specific entity).
 * 
 * @namespace Systematic
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussionboard_settings = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_settingsPayload>
/**
 * Model discussionboard_audit_logs
 * System Audit Log - Records all critical, privileged, moderation, admin, or config actions. Fulfills trace and compliance requirements for role escalation, post deletion, and sensitive changes (see 'Audit & Compliance'). Each log links to the user/id that performed the action and optionally the entity affected. 3NF with atomized actions only; no aggregates, counts, or derived data.
 * 
 * @namespace Systematic
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussionboard_audit_logs = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_audit_logsPayload>
/**
 * Model discussionboard_members
 * Actor entity — Implements the 'User Onboarding & Authentication', 'Posting & Interaction', and 'Roles & Permissions Matrix' requirements. Represents a unique human member of the discussion board system, providing the foundation of the actor domain. Fully normalized (3NF), containing only atomic information directly tied to the member and delegating profile/preferences to separate models. Example usages: authenticating users, referencing post authors, assigning roles. Key relationships: referenced by posts, comments, and role tables. Special rules: Unique per user; deleted_at supports soft deletion and audit.
 * 
 * @namespace Actors
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussionboard_members = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_membersPayload>
/**
 * Model discussionboard_moderators
 * Moderator role assignment — Implements 'Moderator Journey', 'Roles & Permissions Matrix', and 'Moderation & Reporting' requirements. This table grants moderator privileges to selected members, tracking assignment duration and status. Fully normalized: stores only data directly related to the moderator assignment, not member details. Example: assigning John (discussionboard_member_id) as a moderator from 2024-07-24 to 2024-09-01. Key relationship: FK to discussionboard_members. Special: Enforces 1:1 mapping per member, audited by start/end timestamps.
 * 
 * @namespace Actors
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussionboard_moderators = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_moderatorsPayload>
/**
 * Model discussionboard_admins
 * Administrator role assignment — Implements 'Admin Journey', 'Roles & Permissions Matrix', and 'Role Escalation' business rules. Represents users granted full administrative privileges. Contains assignment and status audit details only, normalized away from member records. Usage: assigning/removing admins, enforcing escalations, logging system changes. Key: FK to member, 1:1 mapping. Special: References assignment metadata for security/traceability.
 * 
 * @namespace Actors
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussionboard_admins = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_adminsPayload>
/**
 * Model discussionboard_member_profiles
 * Member profile — Implements 'Profile Setup', 'User Journey', and privacy requirement sections. Contains extended, user-editable profile details (not security/role related), normalized from core member table. Supports flexible addition of non-auth data (display_name, bio, links). Full normalization ensures all profile attributes relate solely to the member's public-facing info, not account details. Example: viewing public member card. FK to member; 1:1. Constraints: Each member has at most one profile record.
 * 
 * @namespace Actors
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussionboard_member_profiles = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_member_profilesPayload>
/**
 * Model discussionboard_member_preferences
 * Member notification and settings preferences — Implements 'Notifications & Updates', 'Accessibility & Usability', and 'User Journey' requirements. Records user-controlled preferences for notifications, UI configuration, and possibly localization settings. Maintains normalization: stores only true user settings, never derived data or cached computations. Example: preference for email notifications true, weekly digests suppressed. FK to member; 1:1 record. Special: nulls permitted for unset defaults.
 * 
 * @namespace Actors
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussionboard_member_preferences = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_member_preferencesPayload>
/**
 * Model discussionboard_boards
 * Board entity - This implements the board management and categorization requirement from the requirements analysis (Business Requirements #2, User Journey #3).
 * 
 * A board represents a single discussion space, usually per broad topic (e.g., Global Economics, Politics). Organizes threads and posts under user-driven topics. Maintains 3NF compliance by ensuring all meta/setting data is separated—actual posts or threads are stored in separate tables/files.
 * 
 * For example, a single 'Political News' board contains many threads, all linked via threads table. Key relationships: links to category, board_settings, section (external); may be moderated by multiple moderators via discussionboard_board_moderators. Special behaviors: Boards may be visible, archived, or require moderation.
 * 
 * @namespace Boards
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussionboard_boards = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_boardsPayload>
/**
 * Model discussionboard_board_categories
 * Board Category entity - Implements the organizational category requirement for grouping boards into top-level classes (Business Requirements #2, Usability).
 * 
 * A category represents a container for related boards (e.g., 'Economics', 'Politics'). Maintains strict 3NF: category only links meta-data; boards linked via FK. For example, a user browsing by category sees all boards for that subject. Key relationships: referenced by boards; never contains board details directly. Special behaviors: Categories may be edited by admins only.
 * 
 * @namespace Boards
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussionboard_board_categories = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussionboard_board_categoriesPayload>
/**
 * Model discussionboard_board_settings
 * Board Settings entity - Implements per-board configuration from business requirements (esp. Admin Journey #3, Board Configurations).
 * 
 * Each record contains settings (not content) for a specific board: various advanced flags and limits central to system operation. Maintains 3NF by completely separating board meta/config from threads/posts. For example, allows a board to require invite-only posting, limit max posts per hour, or toggle advanced features without affecting normal thread data. Key relationships: linked one-to-one to a board; referenced only via FK, not duplicated. Special behaviors: Any schema-altering or configuration parameter not fitting as content goes here. Only editable by admins.
 * 
 * @namespace Boards
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe

### `discussionboard_channels`

Channel Master - Implements the forum partition and board organization from 'Discussion Board Management'. Provides structural root for categorizing boards into high-level channels like 'Politics', 'Economics', etc. Enforces 3NF by avoiding redundancy in boards/posts and enabling scalable navigation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique channel row identifier.
- `code`: Unique channel code for reference in API/config/logic. Example: 'pol', 'econ'. 3NF, unique, enables lookup/automation.
- `name`: Channel name for display and navigation. Example: 'Politics'. User-facing, normalized, not derived.
- `description`: Expanded channel explanation for users. Optional, supports UI clarity/accessibility. Example: 'Debate and analyze global politics.'
- `position`: Channel order in UI or navigation. Integer sequence for manual arrangement—never calculated.
- `active`: Is channel active/visible? Implements archiving/soft-delete logic from requirements. Not derived, enforced atomic.
- `created_at`: Created timestamp for audit trail and debugging.
- `updated_at`: Last modification timestamp for history/compliance.

### `discussionboard_sections`

Section Master - Implements channel subdivision for structured forum hierarchy (Channel → Section → Board). Reduces clutter; 3NF prevents board/post denormalization. Maps to forum topics (Asia, Policy, Announcements, etc). Enforces single-channel constraint—each section must belong to a channel.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique section row identifier.
- `discussionboard_channel_id`: Parent channel's [discussionboard_channels.id](#discussionboard_channels). Strict foreign key; every section is linked to a channel for navigational consistency and data normalization.
- `code`: Unique section code for API/config reference. Example: 'asia', 'us', 'policy'. Not duplicated in boards/posts; ensures normalization.
- `name`: Section name for UI display. Example: 'Asia & Pacific Policy'.
- `description`: Section explanation or summary. Supports contextual browsing/accessibility. Nullable, as some sections may lack details.
- `position`: Section UI order. Manual integer for customizable navigation; atomic, not calculated.
- `active`: Is section visible/enabled? Enables archiving/soft-delete workflows in requirements without deletions. Not derived.
- `created_at`: Section creation timestamp for logs and compliance.
- `updated_at`: Last change timestamp for audit/history.

### `discussionboard_configurations`

System Configuration Store - Implements global/system-level settings and toggles for runtime business flexibility. 3NF, one config per row (no lists/blobs). Used for feature flags, thresholds, and system parameters per requirements. No denormalized summaries; config items managed independently.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique configuration identifier.
- `key`: Setting key (e.g., 'max_post_per_hour'). Used for lookups and automation. One row per config. 3NF enforced by uniqueness.
- `value`: Setting value (always string for flexibility, conversion in app logic). Nullable to support unset/optional configs (e.g., 'true', '5').
- `description`: Human-meaningful description for admin support, UI docs, and compliance. Optional, for clarity/support only.
- `created_at`: Audit field: when the config was created/added.
- `updated_at`: Last modification time for change tracking.

### `discussionboard_notifications`

System Notification Log - Logs every system notification sent for delivery record, debugging, and compliance ('Notifications & Updates', 'Audit & Compliance'). Information is normalized—does not calculate or store aggregate counts. Optionally associates with a user/entity by uuid, never with denormalized info. Does not duplicate status info already elsewhere (only atomic notification row).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique notification log record.
- `target_id`: Entity/user that received the notification (nullable, as not all notifs are personalized). App-resolved; not enforced by DB-level foreign key.
- `type`: Event type (e.g., 'user_mention', 'system_announcement'). Drives notification flows. Not enum, normalized string, not derived.
- `title`: Notification summary title for user display (e.g., 'Your post was reported'). Fulfills clarity/UX requirement.
- `body`: Full notification message. Allows null for status-only notifs (e.g., icon/symbol-only in mobile UI).
- `delivered`: Is notification delivery confirmed? Implements audit flag—not calculated or derived.
- `created_at`: Creation log timestamp—required for audit/sync.
- `delivered_at`: If delivered, the actual delivery timestamp. Nullable as delivery may fail/skip.

### `discussionboard_settings`

Per-Feature/Area Settings Table - Stores specific settings applicable to a context/scope (not global configs). Used for per-channel/section/feature toggles as per 'System Settings' requirements. 3NF, does not duplicate values from configuration. Scoped by id/type (nullable when not tied to a specific entity).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique settings row id.
- `scope_id`: Entity or area identifier for which setting applies. Nullable for global context; referential at app-level only.
- `scope_type`: Scope: identifies type (e.g., 'channel','section','feature_flag'). For app/UI routing. Normalized string.
- `key`: Setting key identifying the individual toggle/option. E.g., 'moderation_policy'. Not redundant vs. global config.
- `value`: Setting value (flag, string, limit, etc). Nullable for unset/optional options.
- `description`: Admin-facing notes/explanations. For docs/audit clarity.
- `created_at`: Created time (audit and config tracing).
- `updated_at`: Modification time (audit and compliance).

### `discussionboard_audit_logs`

System Audit Log - Records all critical, privileged, moderation, admin, or config actions. Fulfills trace and compliance requirements for role escalation, post deletion, and sensitive changes (see 'Audit & Compliance'). Each log links to the user/id that performed the action and optionally the entity affected. 3NF with atomized actions only; no aggregates, counts, or derived data.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Each row is an atomic action/event.
- `actor_id`: Id of member/admin/moderator who performed action. Required so audit is always attributable. Enforced by application logic (typically links to users in the Actors component).
- `target_id`: Id of entity/post/board/etc. affected by the action. Nullable for system/global/infrastructure events.
- `action`: Type/classification of audit event (e.g., 'post_deleted','role_assigned','settings_changed'). For reporting and compliance. Atomic, normalized string.
- `payload`: JSON string/serialized details of event context; e.g., diff, reason, metadata. Nullable for simple events. Not calculated, added by app at the time.
- `created_at`: When the action/event occurred (timestamp, always present for audit).

### `discussionboard_members`

Actor entity — Implements the 'User Onboarding & Authentication', 'Posting & Interaction', and 'Roles & Permissions Matrix' requirements. Represents a unique human member of the discussion board system, providing the foundation of the actor domain. Fully normalized (3NF), containing only atomic information directly tied to the member and delegating profile/preferences to separate models. Example usages: authenticating users, referencing post authors, assigning roles. Key relationships: referenced by posts, comments, and role tables. Special rules: Unique per user; deleted_at supports soft deletion and audit.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique user identifier for this member.
- `username`: Member's unique username for login and display. Implements 'User Onboarding & Authentication' requirements; ensures normalization by preventing direct duplication in profile or role tables. Required, non-nullable. Example: 'civicUser42'.
- `email`: Member's unique, verified email address for authentication and notifications. Implements 'User Onboarding & Authentication' and privacy requirements. Normalization: maintained by separating from profile fields. Example: 'user@email.com'.
- `hashed_password`: Securely stored password hash for authentication (NEVER actual plaintext password). Implements security aspects of 'User Onboarding & Authentication'. Always normalized and never duplicated elsewhere. Required for login; example: 'bcrypt$...'.
- `role`: Current assigned role. Implements 'Roles & Permissions Matrix', designating user's system privilege. Normalization: Single authoritative field. Example: 'member', 'moderator', 'admin'.
- `is_active`: Indicates if the member account is currently active. Used to temporarily disable users (e.g., for bans, unverified accounts). Normalized flag; never pre-computed. Example: true/false.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the member joined the system. Audit and analytics support. Not calculated; single source of truth. Example: '2024-07-24T11:01:24.974+09:00'.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last member data update. Used for audit, profile management, and activity tracking. Always normalized, never derived. Example: '2024-07-25T14:30:00+09:00'.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp for soft deletion of member account, or null if the account is active. Supports audit trail and data erasure. Ensures normalization and compliance with privacy regulations. Example: null or '2024-08-01T09:00:00+09:00'.

### `discussionboard_moderators`

Moderator role assignment — Implements 'Moderator Journey', 'Roles & Permissions Matrix', and 'Moderation & Reporting' requirements. This table grants moderator privileges to selected members, tracking assignment duration and status. Fully normalized: stores only data directly related to the moderator assignment, not member details. Example: assigning John (discussionboard_member_id) as a moderator from 2024-07-24 to 2024-09-01. Key relationship: FK to discussionboard_members. Special: Enforces 1:1 mapping per member, audited by start/end timestamps.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the moderator assignment.
- `member_id`: Target member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Identifies which user is granted moderator privileges.
- `assigned_by_admin_id`: Admin's [discussionboard_admins.id](#discussionboard_admins) who assigned the moderator role. For audit and compliance; always references existing admin.
- `assigned_at`: Timestamp when moderator rights were granted. Implements moderation workflow requirements and audit. Normalized field, set at assignment. Example: '2024-07-24T11:15:00+09:00'.
- `expires_at`: When moderator assignment expires, if temporary; null for permanent. Implements 'Temporary Permissions' business process. Ensures normalization: no derived status. Example: null or cutoff time.
- `revoked_at`: Timestamp moderator rights are revoked, or null if active. Track the duration and revocation events for compliance.

### `discussionboard_admins`

Administrator role assignment — Implements 'Admin Journey', 'Roles & Permissions Matrix', and 'Role Escalation' business rules. Represents users granted full administrative privileges. Contains assignment and status audit details only, normalized away from member records. Usage: assigning/removing admins, enforcing escalations, logging system changes. Key: FK to member, 1:1 mapping. Special: References assignment metadata for security/traceability.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the admin assignment.
- `member_id`: Target member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) with admin access. Direct 1:1 mapping to unique member.
- `assigned_by_admin_id`: Admin's [discussionboard_admins.id](#discussionboard_admins) who performed the admin role assignment. Supports traceable, auditable escalation control. Always references another admin (may reference self if bootstrap).
- `assigned_at`: Timestamp when admin rights were granted. Key for audit trail & compliance with 'Audit Trail' requirements. Example: '2024-07-24T11:20:00+09:00'.
- `revoked_at`: Timestamp of admin privilege revocation, or null if active. Ensures clear audit of all admin escalation events. Example: null or revocation time.

### `discussionboard_member_profiles`

Member profile — Implements 'Profile Setup', 'User Journey', and privacy requirement sections. Contains extended, user-editable profile details (not security/role related), normalized from core member table. Supports flexible addition of non-auth data (display_name, bio, links). Full normalization ensures all profile attributes relate solely to the member's public-facing info, not account details. Example: viewing public member card. FK to member; 1:1. Constraints: Each member has at most one profile record.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each profile.
- `member_id`: Associated member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). 1:1 mapping, unique.
- `display_name`: User-chosen display name. Implements profile setup requirements and user personalization. Example: 'Jane Economist'. Normalized as only present in profile table.
- `bio`: Short member biography/summary. Business: used in member card displays. Optional for privacy. Example: 'Policy researcher and economic writer.'
- `avatar_url`: Profile picture/avatar URI. Sets user identity visually; optional per requirements for privacy/flexibility. Example: 'https://site.com/avatar/abc.png'.
- `location`: Free text user location (city, country). Implements user journey customizations and regional sorting. Example: 'Seoul, Korea'.
- `website_url`: User's website link. Supports networking; optional for privacy and safety. Example: 'https://myportfolio.com'.

### `discussionboard_member_preferences`

Member notification and settings preferences — Implements 'Notifications & Updates', 'Accessibility & Usability', and 'User Journey' requirements. Records user-controlled preferences for notifications, UI configuration, and possibly localization settings. Maintains normalization: stores only true user settings, never derived data or cached computations. Example: preference for email notifications true, weekly digests suppressed. FK to member; 1:1 record. Special: nulls permitted for unset defaults.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for this set of preferences.
- `member_id`: Preferences' owner [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Enforces 1:1 mapping.
- `receive_email_notifications`: Whether the member opts to receive email notifications. Implements 'Notifications & Updates'. Normalized to avoid caching state elsewhere. Example: true/false.
- `receive_push_notifications`: Whether the member allows push notifications. Business: compliance with member preferences for engagement. Normalized, never derived. Example: true/false.
- `preferred_language`: Member's preferred language code (e.g., 'en', 'ko'). Supports 'Accessibility & Usability' and localization requirements. Normalization: only presence, not cached translations. Example: 'en'.
- `dark_mode_enabled`: Member preference for dark mode UI. Implements accessibility requirements. Normalized (single source for UI theme settings). Example: true/false.

### `discussionboard_boards`

Board entity - This implements the board management and categorization requirement from the requirements analysis (Business Requirements #2, User Journey #3).

A board represents a single discussion space, usually per broad topic (e.g., Global Economics, Politics). Organizes threads and posts under user-driven topics. Maintains 3NF compliance by ensuring all meta/setting data is separated—actual posts or threads are stored in separate tables/files.

For example, a single 'Political News' board contains many threads, all linked via threads table. Key relationships: links to category, board_settings, section (external); may be moderated by multiple moderators via discussionboard_board_moderators. Special behaviors: Boards may be visible, archived, or require moderation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique board identifier.
- `discussionboard_board_category_id`: Category for this board's [discussionboard_board_categories.id](#discussionboard_board_categories). Groups boards under categories such as 'Economics' or 'Politics.'
- `discussionboard_section_id`: Section reference for this board's [discussionboard_sections.id](#discussionboard_sections). Sections are higher-level partitions managed in 'Systematic', supporting navigation and access control.
- `name`: Board name - Implements name labeling from requirements. Human-readable board label (e.g., 'US Macro Policy') visible in navigation. Normalization: Name only, localized names managed separately for i18n.
- `code`: Board code - Unique code for programmatic lookup (e.g., 'pol_news'). Used in URLs/routing. Ensures normalization by decoupling identifier from visible name.
- `description`: Short board description - Implements descriptive labeling per User Journey & Usability. Used for tooltips or previews in UI. Ensures normalization by making this field atomic. Example: 'Current events and news in global politics.'
- `is_active`: Whether this board is currently active and can accept new threads/posts. Implements platform-wide board lifecycle from business rules. E.g., set false if archived. Normalizes state transitions via single Boolean atomic value.
- `is_visible`: Whether this board is visible to members. If false, board is hidden from public lists (e.g., for private or staff-only spaces). Supports advanced access control workflows. Normalized as single Boolean flag.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of board creation. Implements requirement for content and board lifecycle audit.
- `updated_at`: Last modification time for the board. Implements requirement for audit trails; enables UI to show freshness.

### `discussionboard_board_categories`

Board Category entity - Implements the organizational category requirement for grouping boards into top-level classes (Business Requirements #2, Usability).

A category represents a container for related boards (e.g., 'Economics', 'Politics'). Maintains strict 3NF: category only links meta-data; boards linked via FK. For example, a user browsing by category sees all boards for that subject. Key relationships: referenced by boards; never contains board details directly. Special behaviors: Categories may be edited by admins only.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique category identifier.
- `name`: Category name. Implements category labeling from requirements. Used in UI menus and filters. Ensures normalization by keeping names atomic. Example: 'Global Economics'.
- `code`: Short unique code for category (e.g., 'econ'). Used for programmatic referencing. Ensures normalization by separating technical from display names.
- `description`: Short description of category. Used as tooltips or previews in UI. Normalizes business logic by isolating display info from operational relationships. Example: 'Boards devoted to global and national economic issues.'
- `position`: Ordering hint for category. Determines sort order in UI. Normalizes ordering logic as atomic per-category value; actual order set by admin. Example: 1 for top, 2 for second-level.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp. Used for audits and ordering.

### `discussionboard_board_settings`

Board Settings entity - Implements per-board configuration from business requirements (esp. Admin Journey #3, Board Configurations).

Each record contains settings (not content) for a specific board: various advanced flags and limits central to system operation. Maintains 3NF by completely separating board meta/config from threads/posts. For example, allows a board to require invite-only posting, limit max posts per hour, or toggle advanced features without affecting normal thread data. Key relationships: linked one-to-one to a board; referenced only via FK, not duplicated. Special behaviors: Any schema-altering or configuration parameter not fitting as content goes here. Only editable by admins.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique setting record identifier.
- `discussionboard_board_id`: Board reference for this settings row's [discussionboard_boards.id](#discussionboard_boards). Each board has exactly one associated settings record; enforced via unique index (1:1).
- `is_locked`: Whether the board is currently read-only (locked down for maintenance/moderation). Implements business rules for moderation/admin locking. 3NF: Atomic flag per board only.
- `require_approval_for_posting`: Whether new thread/posts require moderator/admin approval. Implements business requirements for strict moderation boards. Example: True for high-risk debate boards. 3NF: Atomic per-board policy.
- `max_posts_per_hour`: Rate limiting configuration: maximum allowed new posts per user per hour. Implements platform anti-spam rules from business rules/workflows (#2). 3NF: One per board; enforced in services, not duplicated elsewhere.
- `allow_anonymous_viewing`: Board can be browsed by non-members (logged-out users) if true. Implements accessibility/visibility requirements. 3NF: Atomic viewability policy per board.
- `allow_file_uploads`: Allows users to attach/upload files in this board. Implements extended board rule configuration. 3NF: Atomic setting.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for audit trail and recovery policies.
- `updated_at`: Last settings update date. Used for support/forensics/audit trail in compliance needs.

### `discussionboard_board_moderators`

Board Moderator Membership entity - Implements the many-to-many linkage between boards and moderators (Business Rules, Escalation, Roles #3).

Represents the assignment of one or more moderators (from 'discussionboard_moderators', already in Actors) to one or more boards. Maintains 3NF by offloading the relationship to this junction, not duplicating moderator/board data. For example, a moderator can oversee several boards, and each board can have several moderators. Key relationships: FKs to boards and moderators; enabling moderator reassignment or board cleanup without duplication. Special behaviors: May include an 'is_primary' flag for head moderator and a 'joined_at' timestamp for auditing assignments.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique record representing single board-moderator link.
- `discussionboard_board_id`: Board reference for this assignment's [discussionboard_boards.id](#discussionboard_boards).
- `discussionboard_moderator_id`: Moderator reference for this link's [discussionboard_moderators.id](#discussionboard_moderators).
- `is_primary`: Is this moderator currently primary for the board? Implements workflow for escalations (see Escalation section in requirements). Allows UI to highlight responsible moderator. 3NF: Atomic per-link value, not in main board record.
- `joined_at`: When was this moderator assigned to this board? Implements audit/compliance and appeals workflows. Normalized as timestamp field for ordering assignments and reversals.

Discussion Thread - This implements the core thread entity from business requirements: providing a root container for posts, tags, and timeline organization (ref: 01_business_requirements_discussionboard.md, 02_user_journey_and_use_cases_discussionboard.md). Threads are created by members in specific boards and serve as the main aggregation unit for posts/comments. Strict 3NF compliance: no denormalized or calculated fields, all relationships explicit. Example usage: thread on 'Inflation in 2025' in board 'Macroeconomics'. Key relationships: links to boards and thread authors (members).

Properties as follows:

- `body`: Thread description or leading body content. May be null for threads with only posts. Example: 'Discussion about latest trends...'.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp. Implements timeline, ordering, audit, and moderation controls. Example: '2025-07-24T19:01:24Z'.
- `updated_at`: Last updated timestamp. Changes with edit; informs sorting, audit, and moderation workflow.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp (nullable). Used for retention, restore, and moderation/audit workflows. Null if not deleted, else set to deletion time.

### `discussionboard_thread_snapshots`

Thread Snapshot - Implements versioning/audit trail for full edit and moderation history (see: 04_business_rules_and_workflows_discussionboard.md). 3NF compliance. Each snapshot is a version of the thread’s title/body at a point in time. Example: if a thread is edited, a new snapshot is stored with reason and actor data. Relationships: back-references discussionboard_threads, references editing actor (member/moderator/admin). Snapshots are immutable, supporting rollback and thorough audit.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each snapshot instance.
- `thread_id`: Thread reference. Points to [discussionboard_threads.id](#discussionboard_threads) to record which thread this snapshot belongs to.
- `actor_id`: Actor reference for who made this snapshot. Points to [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members); null if system-generated.
- `title`: Title at this snapshot version. Atomic snapshot of the title for audit/history. Example: 'Initial Title'.
- `body`: Body/content at this version. Enables full rollback/restoration. Example: 'First version with full description.'
- `reason`: Edit/mutation reason: moderator note or inline user edit note. Fulfills audit/compliance needs.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp of snapshot version for precise audit history.

### `discussionboard_thread_tags`

Thread Tag Assignment - Provides M:N relationship between threads and tags for discoverability and content organization (see: content organization requirements). This is a strict 3NF bridge table. Tracks assignment/removal. Each record links a tag to a thread, with assignment/removal timestamps. Example: Marking a thread with 'fiscal-policy'. Key relationships: threads and tags (discussionboard_tags). 

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique for each tagging event.
- `thread_id`: Thread reference. Points to [discussionboard_threads.id](#discussionboard_threads) for M:N tagging.
- `assigned_at`: Assignment timestamp, marking when tag applied. Aids in timeline and audit support.
- `removed_at`: Removal timestamp, allows for full tag history (null if active, otherwise set). Used for audit, moderation, and restoration.

### `discussionboard_posts`

Discussion Board Post — Implements the business requirement for user-generated discussion content and post lifecycle management. Each record represents a single post created by a discussion member under a thread and a board. This maintains 3NF by keeping atomic post attributes and referencing all relationships via foreign keys. Member, thread, board connections ensure correct context. For example, a post with title 'Inflation Impact' by a member in a politics thread.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussionboard_thread_id`: Associated thread's [discussionboard_threads.id](#discussionboard_threads). Represents the thread that this post belongs to for content grouping and navigation.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Author member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Represents who created the post, for authorship, accountability, and permission enforcement.
- `discussionboard_board_id`: Target board's [discussionboard_boards.id](#discussionboard_boards). Indicates the board/category where this post appears, enforcing board-topic structure.
- `title`: Post title, used to identify the topic at a glance. Fulfills requirement for clarity and discoverability. For example: 'Global Trade Policy Updates'.
- `body`: Main post content. Full textual body provided by member. Ensures full normalization, no aggregation. Example: argument, opinion, or news analysis.
- `is_deleted`: Soft-deletion flag; true if logically deleted but present for audit. Part of lifecycle/audit rule compliance. Not a hard deletion field.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp for post, to provide audit trails and ordering.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of the post's latest update, required for version tracking and auditability.

### `discussionboard_post_snapshots`

Post Content Snapshot — Implements the requirement for post version history and audit/compliance. Each snapshot stores the full state of a post at a time (title, body, editor), maintaining 3NF. Enables rollback, review, and transparency. Links to affected post and member who made edit, supporting moderation and appeals.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussionboard_post_id`: Parent post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts), enabling reconstruction of edit/version history.
- `editor_member_id`: Editor member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Null if system or deleted member. Supports full audit and rollback.
- `title`: Snapshot of the post's title at the time of change; supports accurate versioning. Example: 'Initial Title'.
- `body`: Snapshot of full post body at edit time, necessary for rollback and transparency.
- `taken_at`: Timestamp when the snapshot was recorded. Key for reconstructing version timeline.

### `discussionboard_post_votes`

Post Vote — Supports upvote/downvote/business ranking features. 3NF compliance: only atomic per-member per-post records, not tallies. Each record is a single member's vote on a single post. Unique constraint prevents duplicate votes. Example: member upvoting a post.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussionboard_post_id`: Voted post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts).
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Voter's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Member who cast the vote.
- `vote_type`: The vote value: 1 for upvote, -1 for downvote, 0 for neutral/removed. Completely normalized, not aggregate.
- `created_at`: When the vote was cast. Necessary for analytics and audit/compliance.

### `discussionboard_post_reports`

Post Report — Tracks reporting and moderation for compliance requirements. Each record represents a single moderation report against a post, including what, who, and why. Maintains strict normalization: each report is atomic, never aggregate. For example, one member reports a post for abuse, specifying type and optional text. Linked to moderation actions via type id.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussionboard_post_id`: Reported post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts).
- `reporter_member_id`: Reporting member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members).
- `report_type_id`: Type of report [discussionboard_report_types.id](#discussionboard_report_types).
- `description`: Freeform text supplied by reporter for context. Nullable. Example: 'Offensive language.'
- `created_at`: When the report was submitted; required for audit and compliance.

### `discussionboard_post_references`

Post Reference — Implements the requirement for referencing/post linking (content cross-linking, citation, or mention). Keeps each reference atomic (single from-one-to-another relationship); enforces normalization rigorously. Supports reference to posts or threads (polymorphic). Example: A post referencing another post for citation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `source_post_id`: This (source) post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts).
- `target_post_id`: Referenced post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts), can be null for thread/class reference.
- `target_thread_id`: Referenced thread's [discussionboard_threads.id](#discussionboard_threads), can be null for post-only reference.
- `reference_type`: Reference type: 'post', 'thread', or 'comment'. String marker for polymorphic reference; not denormalized. Example: 'post'.

### `discussionboard_comments`

Top-level entity for Comments domain—this implements the requirements for associating structured, version-controlled user comments with threads and posts from the discussion board, as described in the business rules (see requirements: Posting & Interaction, Moderation, Audit). Purpose: To persist individual member-authored comments under posts, enable thread-based discussions, and facilitate moderation. Strict 3NF normalization is maintained—no derived/calculated fields. Example: User Alice replies to a discussionboard_post, creating a new comment entity. Key relationships: links to parent post, authoring member, version history. Special behaviors: Deletion and editing cascade to comment snapshots and votes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each comment record in the table.
- `discussionboard_post_id`: Parent post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts)—connects each comment to its containing post, enabling post-based discussion threading.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Authoring member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members)—identifies who wrote this comment, enforcing accountability and permission checking.
- `parent_id`: Optional self-reference to discussionboard_comments.id for nested (reply) comments, allowing recursive threaded discussions. Null for top-level comments.
- `body`: Main content of the comment. Implements the core posting requirement (3). Ensures normalization by storing only user-authored text per record. For example, the comment: "I disagree with your point because...". No formatting or summary—pure content only.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the comment was created. Implements audit & compliance requirements for tracking comment lifecycle. Example: '2025-07-24T19:01:24.976Z'.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of the latest update (edit). Used for version control/auditing. Enables displaying 'edited' markers. Null if never edited.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-deletion marker for comment removal. Null if active. Implements moderation and user workflow for reversible deletion/auditing. Maintains normalization by separating status from content/body.

### `discussionboard_comment_snapshots`

Snapshot/audit history for comments—implements audit trail and historical versioning for moderation and rollback. Implements requirements: Content Quality Assurance, Moderation Escalation, and audit logs. Purpose: To persist every historical version of a comment whenever it's edited or deleted. Maintains full 3NF normalization by storing immutable versions (no calculated fields). Example: When a comment is edited, a new snapshot is created with prior content/metadata. Key relationships: Links to comment, versioned author, and source post. Special behaviors: Readonly after creation; never updated.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each comment snapshot.
- `discussionboard_comment_id`: Parent comment's [discussionboard_comments.id](#discussionboard_comments)—links each snapshot to the main comment being versioned, facilitating audit trails and historical review.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: The authoring member at the time of this comment version. Implements precise version-era authorship for audit/recovery.
- `discussionboard_post_id`: The parent post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts) at the time of this comment version. Ensures contextual placement of the snapshot even if post-comment relationships evolve.
- `body`: Immutable snapshot of the comment's content at the time of this version. Implements forensic review requirements for moderator/admin oversight. For example, an edited comment retains its original wording here.
- `version`: Monotonic version number assigned to each comment snapshot for the same comment. Implements requirements for traceable edit history and rollback granularity. For example, version 2 = first edit.
- `snapshot_created_at`: Timestamp when the snapshot was created (distinct from the comment's main created_at). Supports ordered audit/review.

### `discussionboard_comment_votes`

Normalized mapping of user upvotes/downvotes on comments—implements Posting & Interaction and Moderation requirements for voting (requirements: 3, 4, 8). Purpose: To enable per-member, per-comment recording of up/down votes without duplication or pre-calculation (fully normalized). Example: When member Alice upvotes a comment, a new row links her to that comment, with the vote direction/score. Special behaviors: Uniqueness constraint prevents duplicate votes; allows updates for toggling/removing votes; no aggregate score is stored here—it must be computed via query or via materialized view.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each comment vote entry.
- `discussionboard_comment_id`: Target comment's [discussionboard_comments.id](#discussionboard_comments)—the comment being voted on.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Voting member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members)—who cast this vote.
- `vote_type`: Stores vote direction for the comment—typically 'up' or 'down' (could use enum at application layer). Implements posting/interaction rule for vote casting. Example: vote_type='up'.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the vote was created/cast. Required for audit and analytics (e.g., changing votes over time).
- `updated_at`: Timestamp for vote changes (e.g., toggling from up to down, or undoing vote). Null if never changed.

### `discussionboard_comment_reports`

Normalized reporting record for moderation/audit—implements requirements for Member moderation participation, Moderation & Reporting workflows, and audit escalation (see requirements: 4, 8). Each record represents one member's report against one comment for a specific reason, referencing report types (already implemented) and moderation flow. Maintains full normalization. Example: When a member reports a comment, a new record is created (with a type, reference to reporting member and targeted comment). Special behaviors: Uniqueness constraint prevents redundant reports by the same member for the same comment and type.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each comment report entry.
- `discussionboard_comment_id`: Target comment's [discussionboard_comments.id](#discussionboard_comments)—the comment being reported for review.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Reporting member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members)—who filed the report.
- `discussionboard_report_type_id`: Type/category of the report, from [discussionboard_report_types.id](#discussionboard_report_types)—e.g., spam, abuse, off-topic (for analytics and escalation flow).
- `reason`: Detailed user-supplied explanation of why the comment is being reported—implements requirements for nuanced moderation case handling and transparency. E.g., "This comment contains hate speech." Null not allowed for accountability.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the report was made. Required for audit trail, moderator SLAs, and activity analysis.

### `discussionboard_reports`

Discussion Board Report Record - Implements the reporting and escalation flow described in the requirements (see 'Business Rules & Workflows,' 'Moderation & Escalation Workflows').

Business Purpose: Captures member-initiated reports on inappropriate content or suspicious users, forming the starting point for moderation review. Maintains 3NF compliance by separating report metadata from other business entities. For example, a member reporting a post or comment for spam or abuse will be registered as a discussionboard_reports entry referencing the reported item and the reporting member.

Key relationships: Connects to report type, target object (via foreign key to posts, comments, or users), and the reporting actor (from already created discussionboard_members table).
Special behaviors: Supports audit trail, links to downstream moderation actions, and enforces one report per object/member per unique incident.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the report record.
- `discussionboard_report_type_id`: Associated report type [discussionboard_report_types.id](#discussionboard_report_types) identifying the reason for report (e.g., spam, abuse, misinformation).
- `reporting_member_id`: The reporting member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) who filed the report.
- `target_object_id`: Target business object being reported (post, comment, or user, as per assignment). The true type is determined by context on review. Implements the polymorphic target pattern in a fully normalized way (all references are UUIDs only).
- `target_object_type`: Type of object being reported. Implements requirement to generalize reporting (e.g., 'post', 'comment', 'member'). Used by moderation workflows to route and describe moderation procedures.
- `report_description`: Reporter supporting detail or description. Implements requirement for explanation or supporting evidence. Maintains normalization: only the specific explanation for this incident.
- `reported_at`: Timestamp of report creation. Implements audit trail and supports compliance/SLA tracking as required by moderation workflow.

### `discussionboard_report_types`

Report Type Registry - Implements the classification of reportable incident subjects (see Business Requirements, Content Quality Assurance, and Moderation documentation).

Business Purpose: Provides an extensible classification system for report reasons (e.g., spam, abuse, misinformation) as required for moderation triage. Maintains 3NF compliance by separating report type code/label definitions from actual reports.

Key relationships: Referenced by discussionboard_reports entries.
Special behaviors: Codes must be unique. Used by the frontend to present selectable reasons for reporting content.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `code`: Short, unique report type code (e.g., 'spam', 'abuse'). Used for frontend and backend logic to reference the report type.
- `display_name`: User-visible name of the report type for UI display.
- `description`: Long-form description for mods/admins. Clarifies what constitutes this report type. Aids in moderation process training.
- `active`: Whether this report type is currently selectable (e.g., deprecated types are marked inactive, for regulatory or policy changes).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this type was created (registry audit trail, required for governance and compliance tracking).

### `discussionboard_moderation_actions`

Moderation Action Record - Implements the 'Action Workflow' and audit requirements specified for both moderators and admins (see Workflows section, Requirement 3: "Moderation & Reporting").

Business Purpose: Tracks every moderation intervention taken in response to reports: edits, deletions, warnings, bans, pin/unpin, locks.

Maintains normalization by linking to the originating report (if any), the acting moderator/admin, and the target object. No pre-calculated summaries or denormalization.

Key relationships: Connects to discussionboard_reports; references acting moderator/admin (otherComponents); links to object of action (via polymorphic pattern).
Special behaviors: Each action includes rationale, timestamps, and type.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each moderation action.
- `report_id`: Associated report [discussionboard_reports.id](#discussionboard_reports) if this action originates from a user report (nullable for proactive/patrol actions).
- `acting_moderator_id`: Acting moderator or admin [or discussionboard_admins.id](#discussionboard_moderators) who performed the action.
- `target_object_id`: Target business object being moderated (post, comment, member, etc.). Same pattern as reports for generalized reference.
- `target_object_type`: Type of object being moderated ('post', 'comment', 'member', 'board', etc.). Maintains the normalized reference per domain context.
- `action_type`: Type of moderation action taken (e.g., 'warn', 'edit', 'delete', 'ban', 'lock', 'pin', etc.). Enables analytics integration for action type filtering.
- `rationale`: Explanation and notes justifying the action. Fulfills requirement for rationale documentation and behavioral transparency. Maintains 3NF (no cross-table references stored here).
- `actioned_at`: Timestamp when the action was performed. Used for audit log, SLA tracking, and analytics.

### `discussionboard_bans`

Ban/Suspension Record - Implements member bans and suspensions per Moderation business rules and workflows (see escalation section, warnings > temp ban > perm ban).

Business Purpose: Captures formal restrictions on members' system access/abilities after infractions are verified. Retains 3NF by referencing the subject (member id), the moderator/admin, and the originating report or rationale (if present).

Key relationships: Links to ban subject (member), acting moderator/admin, and referenced report.
Special behaviors: Multiple bans per member possible if for separate incidents. Each ban is atomic and historical for audit/compliance. Dates track duration and compliance requirements.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `banned_member_id`: The banned member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) subject to ban action.
- `acting_moderator_id`: Moderator/admin [or discussionboard_admins.id](#discussionboard_moderators) who enacted the ban (compliance/audit).
- `report_id`: Originating [discussionboard_reports.id](#discussionboard_reports) if the ban was triggered by a specific report (nullable for proactive major bans).
- `reason`: Ban reason (human-meaningful summary for compliance/audit, visible in appeals workflows).
- `ban_type`: Type: 'temporary' or 'permanent' as per business rules (see moderation escalation workflows).
- `banned_at`: Start datetime of the ban (when enforced).
- `expires_at`: When ban ends (nullable for permanent bans). Maintains normalized structure for expiry logic.

### `discussionboard_warnings`

Warning Issuance Record - Implements the warning step in the moderation escalation pipeline (see Business Rules, "Members receive warnings for policy violations; repeated offenses escalate").

Business Purpose: Records the issuance of official warnings to members, described as the first step in the escalating penalty process. 3NF compliance is maintained by linking each warning to the subject member and the moderator/admin, as well as any originating report. Warnings are atomic events, not aggregated (no counts or derived statuses are stored here).

Key relationships: Related to members (warned_member_id), linked to moderator/admin, and can reference a report.
Special behaviors: Multiple warnings per member are possible; each is an independent event for audit trail and escalation automation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key for each warning record.
- `warned_member_id`: Member who receives the warning [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members).
- `acting_moderator_id`: Moderator/admin issuing the warning [or discussionboard_admins.id](#discussionboard_moderators).
- `report_id`: Report that caused the warning (nullable if warning is preemptive or for off-platform evidence).
- `reason`: Warning reason, descriptive text stating the violation or risk observed. Implements need for clarity and behavioral documentation.
- `warned_at`: Timestamp when warning was applied. Maintains full audit traceability.

### `discussionboard_engagement_metrics`

Tracks post, comment, and voting engagement across users, threads, boards, and time windows. Implements business requirements from analytics use cases (see doc 01 and 02), providing the basis for DAU/WAU charts, cohort analysis, board-level tracking, and moderation metrics. Maintains 3NF by atomically tracking metrics by entity and period, with all pre-calculated/aggregated fields in materialized views only. For example, storing counts of posts, comments, reactions (upvotes/downvotes) per entity per period (e.g., daily). Referenced by analytics dashboards; connects to members, boards, and time periods for detailed engagement breakdowns. Special behaviors: Ensures only raw, non-pre-aggregated, normalized metrics for further processing; NO denormalized fields here.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each engagement metric record.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: The member whose engagement is being recorded. Points to [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) in Actors domain. Supports analytics per user metric.
- `discussionboard_board_id`: The board where engagement occurs. Points to [discussionboard_boards.id](#discussionboard_boards) in Boards domain. Enables board-level metric analysis.
- `engagement_date`: Date for the measured engagement activity. Used for time-bucketed DAU/WAU analysis. Normalization: atomic date, not derived.
- `posts_created_count`: Number of posts created by the referenced member on the board for the day. Implements requirement for tracking post volume. Not pre-aggregated; count is atomic per user/board/date.
- `comments_created_count`: Number of comments created. Supports moderation and content quality metrics.
- `votes_cast_count`: Number of voting actions (upvotes/downvotes) performed by the user on the board in the period. Fulfills analysis requirement for voting engagement.

### `discussionboard_activity_logs`

Stores a normalized, queryable log of analytic events related to member activity across the platform, as required by doc 02 User Journeys and Analytics Use Cases. Implements raw event stream/log for tracking time series activity (e.g., logins, post creations, comment edits, account changes, board visits) for audit and analytics. Maintains 3NF: each row records precisely one event; all aggregation occurs in materialized views. Connected to member, optional thread, board, post, or comment. Used for audit, anomaly detection, rare journey tracking, and engagement heatmaps (e.g., heatmap visualizations of peak platform activity). Special: Enforces normalized, atomic event records (not summary counts).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each activity log record.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Member acting in the event (nullable for system/non-member events). References [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members).
- `discussionboard_board_id`: Board related to the activity (nullable when not board-specific). References [discussionboard_boards.id](#discussionboard_boards).
- `discussionboard_thread_id`: Thread related to the event. Nullable if event is not thread-specific. References [discussionboard_threads.id](#discussionboard_threads).
- `discussionboard_post_id`: Post involved in the event. Nullable unless directly post-related. References [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts).
- `discussionboard_comment_id`: Comment involved in the event. Nullable unless directly comment-related. References [discussionboard_comments.id](#discussionboard_comments).
- `event_timestamp`: Timestamp of the event/action for precise time series and audit. Implements analytics requirements for time-based user activity tracking.
- `event_type`: Type of activity (e.g., 'login', 'logout', 'post_create', 'post_edit', 'post_delete', 'comment_create', 'comment_edit', 'comment_delete', 'vote', 'visit_board', 'ban', 'role_change', 'notification_viewed', etc.) Implements analytics, moderation, and auditing requirements.
- `event_metadata`: Free-form JSON, stringified, with additional event context (device, IP, old/new values, change details, etc.). Implements rare journeys analysis and audit trails.

### `discussionboard_trending_topics`

Tracks active/trending topics (thread/post/title combos) for the trending panel and analytics dashboards. Implements analytics requirements for highlighting trending discussions, detecting viral posts, and displaying platform trends by period. Maintains 3NF: one row per topic per period, with rankings and trend markers computed externally or in mv_ tables (no denormalized fields here). Example: records trending score of a thread in a given day, referenced for homepage highlights. Connected to threads, board; enables detection of surging topics to alert moderation or trigger notifications. Special behaviors: Atomic data only, NO pre-aggregated lists or computed fields.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each trending topic record.
- `discussionboard_thread_id`: Thread considered as trending. References [discussionboard_threads.id](#discussionboard_threads).
- `discussionboard_board_id`: Board under which the trending thread is tracked. References [discussionboard_boards.id](#discussionboard_boards).
- `ranking_period_date`: Date for which the trending status/ranking is recorded. Implements period-based (e.g., daily) tracking of trending status per topic.
- `trending_score`: Quantitative score for the topic's trending calculation—not precomputed, but source score as calculated by external analytics engine or background job. Implements requirement for ordering trending panels. (e.g., engagement-weighted activity score)

### `discussionboard_notification_templates`

Notification Template Entity - This implements the requirement for system-triggered notifications from the requirements document (Business Requirements: 6. Notifications & Updates, 9. Data Privacy & Protection). 

Business explanation: Enables the platform to manage, organize, and version all message templates used for member notifications (email, in-app, browser). Maintains 3NF normalization by splitting templates from notification triggers and user preferences, thus providing single-source for reusable content. For example, a template defines the body for 'Thread Reply', which can then be used by various notification jobs/services. 

Key relationships: No direct foreign keys. Templates are referenced by notification delivery engines and preference settings elsewhere in the system. 
Special behaviors: Supports audit trails, mutable content with unique code per template, version history if needed.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each notification template.
- `code`: Template Code - Implements template identification and enforcement. Business meaning: Unique short string used to reference this template (e.g., 'reply_notification'). Separates template logic from notification event logic, enables auditability by code, and prevents duplicates. Example: Used by notification jobs to fetch rendered content for email or in-app use. Constraint: Must be unique across all templates.
- `name`: Template Name - Implements template user-friendly reference. Business meaning: Human-readable title for each notification template. Ensures normalization by preventing use of business data in multiple places. Example: Shown to admins when configuring notification settings. Constraint: Must not be null.
- `description`: Template Description - Provides extended context for admins. Business meaning: A sentence or two that describes the intent or use-case of the template. Ensures normalization by allowing proper documentation in one place. Example: 'Sent when a user receives a reply to their thread.' Nullable for brevity in simple templates.
- `subject`: Template Subject - Implements message subject customization. Business meaning: Used for email or notification headers. Ensures clear communication and organization. Example: '[DiscussionBoard] New reply to your thread'. Constraint: Not nullable for communication clarity.
- `body`: Template Body - The main message content, possibly with placeholders. Ensures normalization by centralizing source message text for all notification jobs/services. Example: 'Hello {{username}}, your post received a reply...'. May use parameter placeholders for personalization. Not nullable to ensure every template is usable.
- `is_active`: Active Status Flag - Indicates if this template is available for use. Implements enable/disable without deletion for audit trails and error prevention. Example: Deactivating a deprecated or seasonal template. Not nullable.
- `created_at`: Creation Timestamp - Implements audit trail requirement (Business Rules: Section 6). Business meaning: When was the template created. 3NF compliance by storing as atomic value. Not nullable.
- `updated_at`: Update Timestamp - Implements last-modified tracking. Records when the template was last edited. Normalized per audit/compliance guidance. Not nullable.

### `discussionboard_notification_preferences`

Notification Preferences Entity - Implements user-specific notification customization per Business Requirement 6 (Notifications & Updates) and 3 (User Journey & Use Cases). 

Business explanation: Stores each member’s notification channel preferences for different template types (e.g., email, SMS, in-app). Supports compliance with data privacy laws by honoring user opt-in/out settings. Enforces normalization by decoupling per-user/channel rules from system triggers and message templates. Example: User sets 'email' notifications only for mentions, but not for thread replies. 

Key relationships: Links to discussionboard_members via foreign key. References notification template codes for channel granularity. 
Special behaviors: Each (member_id, code) pair must be unique. Allows for per-template and per-channel enable/disable granularity. Audit fields included for compliance.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each notification preference row.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Belonged member’s [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Links notification preference to user account.
- `code`: Notification Template Code - Implements per-template preference setting. Business meaning: Which notification type this preference applies to. Ensures normalization by not embedding template details; only links by code. Not nullable.
- `email_enabled`: Enable for Email - Indicates if the member wants email notifications for this code. Implements granular opt-in control (required for privacy regulations). Not nullable.
- `inapp_enabled`: Enable for In-App - Indicates if in-app/bell notifications are enabled. Business meaning: Supports per-channel enable/disable. Not nullable.
- `browser_enabled`: Enable for Browser Push - Channel preference for browser push notifications. Ensures each user can control channel specificity. Not nullable.
- `created_at`: Creation Timestamp - For audit and compliance tracking. Not nullable.
- `updated_at`: Update Timestamp - Last modified tracking. Ensures temporal auditability. Not nullable.

### `discussionboard_privacy_policies`

Privacy Policy – This model implements the explicit business requirement for transparent privacy and data protection policies outlined in the platform requirements. Each record stores a distinct, time-versioned policy for audit, legal compliance, and user access. Policies are never overwritten, ensuring a full historical audit trail and 3NF normalization. Example: When a new version of the privacy policy is adopted, a new record is inserted; users can access the version effective when they joined.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique policy version identifier. Ensures entity singularity for audit/history.
- `version`: Policy Version – Structured textual identifier (e.g., 'v2024.06') referenced in logs or member consent records. Uniquely identifies each record. Normalized, atomic.
- `effective_date`: Policy Effective Date – When this version of the policy became active. Used for temporal access control and audits. Fully atomic (3NF).
- `title`: Policy Title – Short heading for the policy. Enables user recognition and log referencing. Allows multi-language by separate records.
- `content`: Policy Content – The authoritative text for legal compliance and user review. Only non-calculated, non-redundant full text allowed.
- `created_at`: Created At – Timestamp when this policy version was created in the system. For audit/compliance.
- `updated_at`: Updated At – Last updated timestamp. For change tracking, audit.

### `discussionboard_data_erasure_requests`

Data Erasure Request – Implements the business need for user-initiated account/data deletion and administrator compliance tracking (GDPR/CCPA/etc.). Records each member erasure request, its status, processing timestamps, and rationale. All data is fully normalized (3NF); status/history are atomic, with no pre-calculated aggregates. Key for regulatory audit and platform trust. Example: Members submit erasure requests independently, admins can query and process them, with all changes independently logged. Links to discussionboard_members in Actors by foreign key for referential integrity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each erasure request. Enables audit and traceability.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Belonged member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). FK to Actors component for requestor identity. Fully normalized, ensures direct link to user identity for audit.
- `status`: Request Status: Current disposition of the erasure request (ex: 'pending', 'approved', 'denied', 'completed', etc.). Only the instantaneous status (not calculated) is stored; maintains atomicity for 3NF. Admins or the process flow must update the value as the request advances.
- `requested_at`: Requested At – When the erasure request was created (for auditing, compliance, and metrics). Atomic.
- `reviewed_at`: Reviewed At – When an admin/moderator reviewed the request. Nullable; if never reviewed, stays null. Keeps precise process timestamps normalized.
- `completed_at`: Completed At – When erasure or rejection was completed. Nullable, only present on completion. Strictly atomic for audit and query needs.
- `admin_remark`: Admin Remark – Optional explanatory note for audit/logging (e.g., why approved/denied). Nullable (optional field). Ensures 3NF by separating from status/timestamps.

operations.specification: List all channels for the discussion board system. This operation allows searching and filtering of channels based on their actual fields in the schema: id, code, name, description, position, active, created_at, and updated_at. Supports advanced queries for management, navigation, and analytics. Only references fields present in the Prisma schema discussionboard_channels table. Intended for admins and management UI that needs to view the complete set of channels with potential filters on code, name, active status, or other actual columns. No reference is made to non-existent fields. Pagination, search, and sort may be required by the client as part of this PATCH query. No soft or hard delete logic applies here as this is a list/retrieval endpoint.
operations.description: Retrieves a list of discussion board channels for management or navigation purposes. The API accepts search, pagination, or filtering parameters to find channels by fields such as code, name, and active status. Uses only actual fields in the discussionboard_channels table (id, code, name, description, position, active, created_at, updated_at). No non-existent fields are referenced. Admins or system UI may query using this endpoint to list all channels, preview their metadata, and navigate to their details or further modify them. IPageDiscussionboardConfiguration.description:
설정 리스트의 페이지네이션 컨테이너.

플랫폼 런타임 시스템 설정의 목록을 여러 페이지로 나누어서 반환할 때 사용합니다. 각 설정 레코드는 discussionboard_configurations 테이블의 전체 필드를 포함합니다. pagination 속성에는 현재 페이지 정보, limit, 전체 레코드 수와 페이지 수가 담기며, data 필드는 각 페이지 단위 설정의 배열입니다.

id.description: 설정 레코드의 고유 식별자(UUID).

key.description: 설정의 키명. 필수, 전역 유일. 시스템의 각 기능 또는 속성을 식별하는 명칭. 예:'max_post_per_hour', 'enable_sms_notice'

oneOf.description:

description.description: 설정에 대한 설명/메모. 관리자에게만 표시되며, 설정 목적이나 사용법에 대한 메타데이터를 제공합니다.

필수/필요 데이터만 포함: key(유일), value(문자열/nullable), description(설명). 생성 일시/수정 일시는 자동 생성됨.

key.description: 생성할 설정의 고유 키(유일). 시스템 기능 식별자 역할을 하며, 비워둘 수 없음.

oneOf.description: 설정 값. string만 허용. null은 미설정 상태로 저장될 수 있음.
설정 값. string만 허용. null은 미설정 상태로 저장될 수 있음.

값(value) 또는 description(설명) 속성만 수정 가능. key 및 id는 변경 불가(불변 속성). 값 적용시 비어 있을 경우 null로 저장.

oneOf.description: 수정할 설정 값. 문자열 또는 null.

상세 설명(메모란) 변경값(옵션).

discussionboard_notifications 테이블에 정의된 필드(target_id, type, title, delivered, created_at 등)에 기반하여 전체/부분 검색, 페이징, 정렬, 기간 필터 등이 가능합니다.

id.description: 알림 로그별 고유 UUID. 단일 조회/특정 타겟 검색 등에서 활용.

target_id.description: 알림을 수신한 엔티티(유저, 채널 등)의 UUID. 개인화된 알림/특정 타겟 알람 필터 시 사용.

type.description: 알림 이벤트 종류명. 예:'system_announcement', 'user_mention', 'ban', 'reply_created' 등과 같이 플랫폼 내 발생 이벤트에 따라 값이 지정됨.

delivered.description: 전달 상태 플래그. true(배달 완료), false(미전달/대기 상태)로 분류. 전달여부 필터링 시 활용.

created_at.description: 알림 레코드가 생성된 시간(ISO-8601). 기간 검색, 최신 정렬, 슬랙/푸시 연동 시 활용.

oneOf.description: 실제 전달 완료 시각(ISO-8601, null 허용). 배달 실적 필터링 등에 사용.

delivered_at.description: 실제 전달 완료 시각(ISO-8601, null 허용). 배달 실적 필터링 등에 사용.

IPageIDiscussionboardNotification.description:
알림 로그 엔티티의 페이지네이션 컨테이너 타입.

discussionboard_notifications 내 알림 로그 레코드들을 배열로, 전체 페이지/레코드 정보를 pagination 속성에 분리하여 제공합니다. 시스템/관리 UI, 개인 알림 리스트 응답, 크로스 플랫폼 알림 로그 analytics 등에서 활용됩니다.

IDiscussionboardNotification.description:
discussionboard_notifications 테이블의 알림 로그 개별 행 모델.

특정 사용자의 알림 내역, 시스템 통지, 배달 상태감시 등에서 개별적으로 조회/분석/발행 내역 추적을 위해 활용됩니다.

레코드의 속성별 설명은 다음과 같습니다.

id.description: 알림 로그 개별 행 고유 UUID

oneOf.description: 알림을 전달받은 대상을 식별하는 UUID (개인화/특정 엔티티/채널/유저 등).
알림을 전달받은 대상을 식별하는 UUID (개인화/특정 엔티티/채널/유저 등).

target_id.description: 알림을 전달받은 대상을 식별하는 UUID (개인화/특정 엔티티/채널/유저 등).

type.description: 알림 이벤트 종류. 예시:'system_announcement', 'user_mention', 'post_reply' 등. UI, 분류, 통계, 알림 처리 등에서 사용.

title.description: 알림 제목 요약. 메인 알림 센터/목록/푸시 표시시 대표 문구.

oneOf.description: 알림의 전체 상세 내용 문자열. null 허용.
알림의 전체 상세 내용 문자열. null 허용.

body.description: 알림의 전체 상세 내용 문자열. null 허용.

delivered.description: 알림 실제 배달여부. True(배달 완료), False(미전달/실패/지연/임시저장 등). 통계/관리/재시도 처리시에 활용.

created_at.description: 알림이 생성된 UTC 기준 시각. 플랫폼 관리/개인 알림 히스토리/audit에서 사용.

oneOf.description: 실제 배달 완료된 전체 타임스탬프(없으면 null). 전달 상태 통계에 사용.
실제 배달 완료된 전체 타임스탬프(없으면 null). 전달 상태 통계에 사용.

delivered_at.description: 실제 배달 완료된 전체 타임스탬프(없으면 null). 전달 상태 통계에 사용.

IDiscussionboardNotification.ICreate.description:
새로운 알림(notification) 로그 행(레코드) 생성 요청 스키마.

필수 생성 속성은 type(이벤트 유형), title(제목), delivered(배달 상태), created_at(생성시각)입니다. target_id 및 body, delivered_at은 옵션으로 선택 적용 가능. 주의: created_at 및 delivered 값은 반드시 백엔드/서비스에서 할당, 관리됩니다.

type.description: 생성될 알림의 이벤트 종류(정의된 string, 예:'system_announcement', 'reply_posted').

title.description: 알림 제목. UI 리스트 및 개인 inbox 등에서 메인 문구로 노출.

oneOf.description: 상세 알림 본문. null 허용. 일반 텍스트 기반, 길이 제한은 서비스 정책에 따름.
상세 알림 본문. null 허용. 일반 텍스트 기반, 길이 제한은 서비스 정책에 따름.

body.description: 상세 알림 본문. null 허용. 일반 텍스트 기반, 길이 제한은 서비스 정책에 따름.

delivered.description: 이 알림이 배달 완료 상태로 바로 생성되는 경우 true, 큐 대기/미전달상태로 생성 시 false. (백엔드 논리에 따라 자동 셋팅 권장)

created_at.description: 생성시각(서버단에서 ISO-8601 기준으로 할당).

oneOf.description: 알림 타겟의 UUID. 알림 개인화/특정 엔티티 대상으로 발행하는 경우에만 사용.
알림 타겟의 UUID. 알림 개인화/특정 엔티티 대상으로 발행하는 경우에만 사용.

target_id.description: 알림 타겟의 UUID. 알림 개인화/특정 엔티티 대상으로 발행하는 경우에만 사용.

oneOf.description: (옵션) 실제 배달 완료 시각. 배달 즉시 발생 케이스 외에는 null 또는 생략.
(옵션) 실제 배달 완료 시각. 배달 즉시 발생 케이스 외에는 null 또는 생략.

delivered_at.description: (옵션) 실제 배달 완료 시각. 배달 즉시 발생 케이스 외에는 null 또는 생략.

IDiscussionboardNotification.IUpdate.description:
알림 로그 행의 값 갱신/수정 요청용 오브젝트(Partial Update/PUT).

수정 가능 속성: type(이벤트 종류), title(제목), body, delivered, delivered_at, target_id(옵션), 기타 null 허용 가능 필드 포함. created_at은 수정 불가/불변 속성.

title.description: 알림 제목.

oneOf.description: 상세 본문 텍스트 문자열. null 허용.
상세 본문 텍스트 문자열. null 허용.

body.description: 상세 본문 텍스트 문자열. null 허용.

delivered.description: 상태 플래그 값. True(배달 완료), False(큐 대기/에러/누락/임시저장).

oneOf.description: 실제 배달 완료 타임스탬프. null 가능.
실제 배달 완료 타임스탬프. null 가능.

delivered_at.description: 실제 배달 완료 타임스탬프. null 가능.

oneOf.description: 대상 타겟(UUID).
대상 타겟(UUID).

IDiscussionboardSetting.IRequest.description:
디스커션보드 기능/area별 설정 레코드(discussionboard_settings) 조회, 필터, 페이징 요청 오브젝트.

scope_id, scope_type, key, value, description, 생성/수정일 필터 지원. 'discussionboard_settings'의 실제 컬럼 기준으로만 검색/정렬/조회 가능. 보통 관리자 UI의 기능 토글, 채널/섹션별 설정 등의 조회에 활용됨.
