username.description:
The member's unique username used for login and display within the discussion board system.

This property maps to the `username` field in the `discussionboard_members` Prisma schema. Changing this value will update the username used throughout the forum. Must be unique and is subject to application and database constraints. Example: 'civicUser42'.

Updating requires appropriate validation to ensure uniqueness and conformance with business rules.

email.description:
The member's unique email address, used for authentication, notifications, and system communication.

Matches the `email` field in the `discussionboard_members` schema. All email addresses must be verified and unique for both authentication and notification compliance. Example: 'user@email.com'.

Changing the email may have implications for account recovery and notification delivery.

role.description:
The role assigned to the member, which defines permissions and capabilities within the system (e.g., 'member', 'moderator', 'admin').

Directly corresponds to the `role` field in the schema. Determines the scope of actions a user can perform, such as posting, moderating, or managing the system.

Any role change should be auditable and comply with escalation protocols.

is_active.description:
Indicates whether the user account is currently active (true) or disabled (false).

Implements the `is_active` field in the Prisma schema, controlling access to the platform. Used for bans, suspensions, and compliance with business rules for user access.

Set to false to disable account access without deleting the member's data.

IBoard.description: Board entity representing a single forum board in the discussion board system. Fulfills discussion space and organization business requirements. Fully normalized (3NF) as per Prisma schema, this entity maps 1:1 with the discussionboard_boards table, exposing only atomic board data and referential fields for use in navigation, thread listing, and management flows.

discussionboard_board_category_id.description: Unique identifier for the board category to which this board belongs. This value should correspond to the actual UUID of a category row in the discussionboard_board_categories table. This field is required to maintain proper board organization and ensure referential integrity within the system. Example: 'a29c6e1f-0a03-4ad3-9d07-cc019cac1019'.

discussionboard_section_id.description: Unique identifier for the section (from discussionboard_sections) that contains this board. This field enables precise navigation and categorization. It must be a valid existing UUID value. Example: 'b3328e2e-4b4f-4be2-8e82-f57dd6d25e02'.

name.description: Human-readable board name used for display in navigation, UIs, and search. Names should follow platform guidelines for topic clarity and length. Example: 'Global Economics'.

code.description: Unique code identifier for this board, suitable for URLs, routing, and programmatic lookup. Code uniqueness is enforced per table constraints and must never be duplicated. Example: 'macro_policy'.

oneOf.description: Optional short description for this board. Provides additional context in tooltips, list previews, and accessibility features. May be null. Example: 'International analysis and discussion of macroeconomic policy.'

Optional short description for this board. Provides additional context in tooltips, list previews, and accessibility features. May be null. Example: 'International analysis and discussion of macroeconomic policy.'

is_active.description: Flag indicating whether this board is currently accepting new threads and posts. 'true' means active; 'false' means the board is archived or closed.

is_visible.description: Boolean flag controlling whether the board is listed to users for navigation and thread creation. 'true' reveals the board to users; 'false' hides it, often used for private, internal, or staff-use boards.

IPageIdiscussionboard_post_votes.description:
Paginated result for post vote entities. This object represents a single page of post votes, commonly used in post interaction analytics or user engagement dashboards for political/economic discussion boards.

The schema aligns with the underlying business rules for normalized, non-aggregated atomic votes (upvote/downvote actions). Pagination metadata facilitates navigation and batch processing in UI or API integrations, and the items array contains vote records always linked to posts and members by their UUID.

All property descriptions are strictly derived from the discussionboard_post_votes table in the Prisma schema.

data.description: List of atomic vote records for this page of results, strictly referencing the post_vote schema.

pagination.description: Pagination information, indicating current page, total pages, result count, etc.

Idiscussionboard_post_votes.description:
Atomic upvote/downvote/neutral record for a single member on a post.

Implements audit, analytics, and voting business rules for the political/economic discussion board. Each row in this entity records a voting action for one user on a specific post, with strict one-vote-per-(user,post) constraint. Didactic for interaction metrics and reputation systems.

This type's properties mirror the columns in Prisma's discussionboard_post_votes table.

id.description: Primary key. Unique identifier of the vote row. Matches discussionboard_post_votes.id.

discussionboard_post_id.description: References the post being voted on. Foreign key to posts. Follows discussionboard_post_votes.discussionboard_post_id.

discussionboard_member_id.description: References the voting member. Uniqueness constraint: one vote per (user,post) pair. Matches discussionboard_post_votes.discussionboard_member_id.

vote_type.description: Vote type: 1 for upvote, -1 for downvote, 0 for neutral/removed. Only these normalized integer values are allowed.

created_at.description: Timestamp of when the vote was cast. Used for analytics/compliance. Matches discussionboard_post_votes.created_at.

Idiscussionboard_post_votes.ICreate.description:
Type for creation of a post vote entity. Represents structure for vote-casting APIs. All required fields correspond to creation columns in the Prisma schema.

No aggregates, soft delete, or audit fields permitted in input. Only atomic fields matching the table's definition.

For upvote: vote_type=1, for downvote: vote_type=-1, for neutral: vote_type=0.

discussionboard_post_id.description: Target post for voting (FK to posts table).

discussionboard_member_id.description: Member casting the vote (FK to members table).

created_at.description: Timestamp for the cast vote. Normally set to now, but may be backfilled for analytics import.

Idiscussionboard_post_votes.IUpdate.description:
Type for updating a post vote entity. Used when revising vote_type (e.g., changing from upvote to downvote), or correcting vote timestamps for analytics/tracing.

All properties directly mirror the columns in discussionboard_post_votes table, except id (which is immutable).

Does not accept non-schema properties or aggregates. Only allows update of atomic vote row data.

discussionboard_post_id.description: Target post for voting (FK to posts table).

discussionboard_member_id.description: Voting member id (FK to member).

created_at.description: Timestamp for the cast vote.

Idiscussionboard_post_reports.description:
Atomic report record for moderation/analytics in the discussion board. One report per (member, post, report type).

Implements audit, reporting, and escalation workflows; referenced by moderation logs and workflows that result in warnings, bans, or deletions.

Fully schema-aligned to discussionboard_post_reports table.

id.description: Unique, atomic report id.

discussionboard_post_id.description: Id of the post being reported (FK).

reporter_member_id.description: Member id who made the report.

report_type_id.description: Type of report (e.g., spam, abuse, off-topic).

oneOf.description: Freeform description given by reporting member; can be empty/null.

description.description: Freeform description given by reporting member; can be empty/null.

Idiscussionboard_post_reports.ICreate.description:
Type for creating a post report entity. Used in reporting workflows, member-flagging of posts. Only atomic schema fields are allowed; reporting business rules enforced at API/service layer.

No soft/hard delete, audit fields, or aggregates included. Strictly primal schema-row creation body. Only member, post, report_type, description (optional), and timestamp.

oneOf.description: Explanation given by member. Nullable for minimal-context cases.

description.description: Explanation given by member. Nullable for minimal-context cases.

created_at.description: Timestamp the report was submitted (audit trail).

IPostReport.IUpdate.description:
Type for updating a post report. Used for correcting reporting mistakes or changing the report details after submission (in audit/appeal cases). Only allows update of atomic schema fields for a report row.

Aligns strictly to the fields in discussionboard_post_reports table except for id (which is immutable). Description can be changed or set to null.

reporter_member_id.description: The member's id who submitted the report.

report_type_id.description: Type/category of the report (as per system codes).

description.description: Updated explanation for the report (can be blank/null).

IPostReport.description:
Post report entity, for moderation, audit, and analytics in the platform.

Represents a single atomic record corresponding to a complaint/report against a post, including reason/type and reporter info. 

Schema strictly mirrors the atomic columns of discussionboard_post_reports.

discussionboard_post_id.description: The post being reported.

oneOf.description: Reporter explanation of infraction or details (nullable).

description.description: Reporter explanation of infraction or details (nullable).

IPostReference.IRequest.description:
Type for search/pagination when querying post reference records—i.e., relations showing citations, cross-links, or replies linking posts and/or threads.

Properties strictly reflect columns present in discussionboard_post_references table.

Does not handle non-existent aggregates, audit status, or delete fields.

target_post_id.description: Target post id (the referenced/cited post in the relationship).

target_thread_id.description: Target thread id (if the reference points to a thread rather than another post).

reference_type.description: Type of reference: accepted schema string for type (e.g., post, thread, comment).

IPageIPostReference.description:
Paginated result for post reference entities—records denoting citations or cross-links between posts or threads.

Each page object contains the array of post reference records and standard AutoBE paging metadata.

Data structure and all fields strictly follow Prisma schema for M:N post linking.

data.description: List of post reference entities (atomic links between posts/threads).

pagination.description: Pagination metadata for result set navigation.

IPostReference.description:
The IPostReference type defines a reference relation between posts and optionally threads within the political/economic discussion board platform.

This aligns with the discussionboard_post_references table of the Prisma schema. Each reference serves as a normalized, atomic relationship, supporting workflows for citations, cross-links, and navigation among user posts and threads. It follows strict 3NF: each row is a single reference/link only, no pre-calculated/aggregate. Used in citation UIs, tracebacks, audit trails, and automated moderation tasks.

Consult the schema: id, source_post_id (required), target_post_id (nullable), target_thread_id (nullable), reference_type (required: e.g., 'post','thread','comment'). All UUIDs.

Created or updated by members, moderators, or admin as system and business process evolves.

id.description:
Primary key identifying each reference link (discussionboard_post_references.id).

A UUID for entity singularity and referential integrity. Used for audits, moderation, or direct access by UI components.

source_post_id.description:
The referencing (source) post's UUID (discussionboard_post_references.source_post_id).

Indicates the post where the reference originates. Required, never null. Enforces referential integrity, enables tracebacks/citations.

oneOf.description:
Referenced (target) post UUID (discussionboard_post_references.target_post_id).

Nullable: if the reference is to a thread only, this may be null. If present, must refer to existing post. Supports polymorphic linking.

Referenced (target) post UUID (discussionboard_post_references.target_post_id).

Nullable: if the reference is to a thread only, this may be null. If present, must refer to existing post. Supports polymorphic linking.

target_post_id.description:
Referenced (target) post UUID (discussionboard_post_references.target_post_id).

Nullable: if the reference is to a thread only, this may be null. If present, must refer to existing post. Supports polymorphic linking.

oneOf.description:
Referenced (target) thread UUID (discussionboard_post_references.target_thread_id).

Nullable: if the reference is strictly to a post, this is null. Enables polymorphic post/thread relationships for advanced citation or content navigation.

Referenced (target) thread UUID (discussionboard_post_references.target_thread_id).

Nullable: if the reference is strictly to a post, this is null. Enables polymorphic post/thread relationships for advanced citation or content navigation.

target_thread_id.description:
Referenced (target) thread UUID (discussionboard_post_references.target_thread_id).

Nullable: if the reference is strictly to a post, this is null. Enables polymorphic post/thread relationships for advanced citation or content navigation.

reference_type.description:
String marker designating the type of reference ('post','thread','comment').

Essential for polymorphic handling of reference relationships. Must be one of the designated values, enforced application-side. Used for moderation, UI differentiation or analytics tracking.

IPostReference.ICreate.description:
Request schema for creating a post reference row.

Follows the discussionboard_post_references model: source_post_id (required), reference_type (required), with optional target_post_id and target_thread_id for polymorphic reference. Used by members, moderators, or automation to register contextual links/citations among content items. All UUIDs must be verified for referential existence prior to creation.

source_post_id.description: UUID of the origin/source post. Must exist in posts table. Required for all reference creation.

oneOf.description: Optional: UUID of the target post. Null if the reference is exclusively to a thread.
Optional: UUID of the target post. Null if the reference is exclusively to a thread.

target_post_id.description: Optional: UUID of the target post. Null if the reference is exclusively to a thread.

oneOf.description: Optional: UUID of the target thread. Null if not applicable.
Optional: UUID of the target thread. Null if not applicable.

target_thread_id.description: Optional: UUID of the target thread. Null if not applicable.

reference_type.description:
Reference type label: 'post', 'thread', or 'comment', as per content domain.

Crucial for enabling flexible UI/logic at creation time. Examples: 'post','thread','comment'.

IPostReference.IUpdate.description:
Schema for updating an existing post reference entity by id.

Allows altering the target relationship or reference type, supporting content reclassification, moderation, or curation workflows. All fields are optional for PATCH-style partial updates, but at least one must be supplied for any update to occur.

Field values must match the Prisma schema: target_post_id, target_thread_id, reference_type. Id is implied by the request path; not changeable via the body.

Optionally update the target post for the reference. Null means remove the post linkage.

Optionally assign or change the target thread. Null if removing thread relationship.

target_thread_id.description: Optionally assign or change the target thread. Null if removing thread relationship.

IComment.IRequest.description:
Parameters for searching, filtering, and paginating comments (discussionboard_comments entity).

Complies with the 'IComment.IRequest' convention used in listing API endpoints. All parameter names must align with the actual column names and types in the Prisma schema discussionboard_comments. Includes support for parent_id (threaded/nested reply), post id, member id, text search on content/body, creation or update window, and deleted_at (for soft-delete workflow compliance).

This type is used by admin, moderator, or UI querying functions.

discussionboard_member_id.description: Comment author's UUID. Enables filtering all comments by (or from) a specific member.

If supplied, lists only direct replies to target comment (for threaded/nested structure). Null for top-level.

created_at_to.description: Filters for comments created before or at this timestamp (inclusive).

updated_at_to.description: Filters for comments last updated on/before this value. Used to limit history search windows.

Sort ordering: ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') for each ordered column.

sort_order.description: Sort ordering: ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') for each ordered column.

data.description: List of comment entities on this page (see IComment for schema detail).

IComment.description:
Schema for an atomic comment entity in the discussionboard_comments table.

Represents a user/member's comment, reply, or moderator/in-system note attached to a post, supporting full moderation, discussion threading, and audit workflows. 100% aligns with Prisma schema: id, discussionboard_post_id, discussionboard_member_id, parent_id (nullable), body, created_at, updated_at (nullable), deleted_at (nullable).

Each instance is one comment attached to a single post, optionally replying to another comment (parent_id). For every historical comment/editable, see ICommentSnapshot for history. Used by member UIs, admin tools, audit logs, and analytics dashboards.

id.description: Primary key for the comment entity (discussionboard_comments.id). A unique, unchanging identifier.

discussionboard_post_id.description:
UUID of the post to which the comment is attached (discussionboard_comments.discussionboard_post_id).

Ensures referential integrity, facilitates post-level threading, and supports reply hierarchies.

discussionboard_member_id.description:
UUID of the comment's authoring member (discussionboard_comments.discussionboard_member_id).

Enables attributions, moderation, and reply functions. Ensures direct relationship with user records.

oneOf.description:

IDiscussionboardCommentSnapshot.IRequest.description:
Filtering/search request for list or history endpoints on comment snapshots (discussionboard_comment_snapshots domain).

snapshot_created_to.description: Filters for snapshots created before this timestamp (inclusive).

IDiscussionboardCommentSnapshot.description:
Atomic entity representing a snapshot (edit/history event) of a comment in discussionboard_comment_snapshots.

Each instance stores a version of a comment's text/body at a specific edit or audit event — immutable retrospective for audit, rollback, moderation, and appeals. Matches schema: id (PK), discussionboard_comment_id (FK), discussionboard_member_id (author at edit), discussionboard_post_id (context), body (historical comment string), version (monotonic edit number), snapshot_created_at (timestamp of history event). Used by audit, version control, and appeals/review processes.

id.description: Snapshot entity PK (discussionboard_comment_snapshots.id). Referenced for audit, rollback, or display.

discussionboard_comment_id.description: FK to the comment entity this is a history for (discussionboard_comment_snapshots.discussionboard_comment_id).

discussionboard_member_id.description: Who authored this comment version at the time (FK to member).

discussionboard_post_id.description:
Post context for the comment snapshot (FK to post).

Used when cross-checking history/audit trails.

body.description: Immutable historical text/body stored at this version of the comment.

version.description: Which edit/version this is for the comment; monotonic for rollback, UI audit, and fraud detection.

snapshot_created_at.description: Timestamp when this version/snapshot event was recorded (audit, rollback, moderation).

IDiscussionboardCommentSnapshot.ICreate.description:
Payload type for creating a new comment snapshot (version history record) in discussionboard_comment_snapshots.

Required properties: discussionboard_comment_id, discussionboard_member_id, discussionboard_post_id, body (text at the time), version, snapshot_created_at (timestamp of snapshot creation). Used by audit, rollback, moderation, and appeals. All properties validated for FK existence before creation.

Represents an atomic moderation event (edit, delete, warn, ban, etc.) as captured in the audit log. Every action is linked to the actor, target, action rationale, and relevant context, supporting compliance and full auditability. Structure exactly matches the Prisma table discussionboard_moderation_actions.

Moderation actions are critical for ensuring transparency, supporting member appeals, and integrating with analytic workflows.

action_type.description: Type of moderation action (e.g., 'warn', 'edit', 'delete', 'ban', 'lock', etc). Business context must define expected values. Free string, not scoped as enum.

rationale.description: Human-readable explanation/reason for taking this moderation action. Critical for audit trail and member appeals.

actioned_at.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC recommended) when moderation action occurred.

IDiscussionboardDataErasureRequest.description:
Data erasure request entity representing a user's formal request for account/data deletion in the political/economic discussion board platform (refer to discussionboard_data_erasure_requests table).

This type includes complete, fully normalized tracking for audit, compliance, and privacy workflows. It captures the lifecycle of a request (submission, review, completion), references the requesting member, and stores timestamps for each process stage. The design ensures alignment with regulatory requirements (e.g., GDPR) and allows platform administrators to manage member requests transparently, log processing history, and document rationale for decisions. All properties strictly conform to the underlying Prisma schema.

Serves use cases such as: member-initiated deletion, platform privacy report generation, admin review queues, and audit trail lookup. All properties trace a single erasure workflow, supporting both user- and admin-managed transitions. No additional, non-schema fields or workflows exist in this definition.

id.description:
Primary key identifier for the data erasure request. Uniquely identifies each erasure submission, allowing reliable lookup for audit, compliance, and workflow management.

Must be a valid UUID format. Assigned on request creation. Used internally for all cross-entity references to this request.

discussionboard_member_id.description:
Foreign key to the member account initiating the erasure request. Points to discussionboard_members.id, ensuring referential integrity.

This property guarantees that each erasure submission is directly attributable to a specific user/member account, fulfilling audit and compliance requirements for traceability. Must always match a valid member id.

status.description:
Current status of the data erasure request. Reflects its workflow progress: 'pending', 'approved', 'denied', 'completed', or other platform-defined values.

Controls access, editability, and triggers for subsequent business processes. Only the instantaneous status is stored—no derived or computed states. String values must align with business logic for request state transitions.

requested_at.description:
Timestamp when the member submitted the data erasure request. Must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time string.

Used for ordering, SLA measurement, and compliance auditing. Cannot be updated after initial creation; establishes the audit trail for regulatory reporting and timeline analysis.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when an admin, moderator, or authorized reviewer first opened, viewed, or acted upon the request in the management interface.

Nullable—remains null when the request has not yet been reviewed, set by the system when review action occurs. Enables compliance with prompt/efficient handling standards and audit requirements.

reviewed_at.description:
Timestamp when an admin, moderator, or authorized reviewer first opened, viewed, or acted upon the request in the management interface.

Nullable—remains null when the request has not yet been reviewed, set by the system when review action occurs. Enables compliance with prompt/efficient handling standards and audit requirements.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when the erasure process was completed or finalized, either by deletion, rejection, or other terminal state.

Nullable—unpopulated if the request has not yet reached completion. Set when admin workflow is finished; used for legal documentation and audit trails.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp when the erasure process was completed or finalized, either by deletion, rejection, or other terminal state.

Nullable—unpopulated if the request has not yet reached completion. Set when admin workflow is finished; used for legal documentation and audit trails.

oneOf.description:
Admin- or moderator-supplied comment describing rationale, notes, or compliance explanation for the disposition of the request.

May be null (optional); included for audit trails, policy transparency, and communication during review/approval/denial workflow. Especially important in compliance or appeal/complaint cases. No computed or derived metadata.

admin_remark.description:
Admin- or moderator-supplied comment describing rationale, notes, or compliance explanation for the disposition of the request.

May be null (optional); included for audit trails, policy transparency, and communication during review/approval/denial workflow. Especially important in compliance or appeal/complaint cases. No computed or derived metadata.

IDiscussionboardDataErasureRequest.IUpda.description:
Payload for updating a data erasure request record in the platform audit and privacy compliance workflow. Corresponds to the mutable fields in the discussionboard_data_erasure_requests Prisma schema.

Supports administrative or moderation workflows that change the state or metadata of a request (status updates, review completion timestamps, admin remarks, etc).

Strictly limited to fields that are updateable post-creation, as defined by 3NF normalization practices. This variant is required for administrative review interfaces, SLA compliance, and compliance documentation. All updates must be auditable and reference compliant values. No creation-only, immutable, or non-schema fields are permitted in this type.

status.description: Latest status for this erasure request. Reflects allowed business state transitions (e.g., 'pending' → 'approved'/'denied'/'completed'). Always a valid state string known to the backend/business logic. Updating status is a privilege reserved for admin/mod roles during review.

oneOf.description: Timestamp of when the data erasure request was reviewed by an administrator/moderator. Value must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time or null if not yet reviewed. Used for audit/logging/SLAs; updatable post initial submission.

reviewed_at.description: Timestamp of when the data erasure request was reviewed by an administrator/moderator. Value must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time or null if not yet reviewed. Used for audit/logging/SLAs; updatable post initial submission.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when the erasure process was marked complete (either executed or administratively closed). Must be ISO 8601 date-time or null if not yet completed. Used for compliance deadlines, platform reporting, and audit trail.

completed_at.description: Timestamp when the erasure process was marked complete (either executed or administratively closed). Must be ISO 8601 date-time or null if not yet completed. Used for compliance deadlines, platform reporting, and audit trail.

oneOf.description: Optional comment from admin/mod explaining review decision, compliance rationale, or communication to the member. Freeform string; null if omitted.

admin_remark.description: Optional comment from admin/mod explaining review decision, compliance rationale, or communication to the member. Freeform string; null if omitted.

scenario.draft: Test admin ability to list discussion board channels using search and pagination filters. Verify correct results when filtering by code, name, description, position, active status, created_at, and updated_at. Check that pagination works as expected when specifying page size and page number. Confirm that channels with both active=true and active=false can be located. Include edge cases where no channels match the filter, and where results cross page boundaries. Failures include invalid filter values or unauthorized access attempt.

Verify that searching for channels with filters that do not match any records returns an empty list, not an error. For example, filter with a unique, non-existing name or code string. Confirm that the response structure is consistent and paginated, but contains no data rows.

Confirm that a non-admin or unauthenticated user is denied access to the channel listing endpoint. Attempt to call the endpoint without admin role and validate that the proper authorization error is returned.

Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of administrator assignments from the system. Simulate use by an admin managing platform access or conducting an audit. Provide search/filter criteria such as assigned_by_admin_id or a specific time range, and verify that the endpoint correctly returns only those assignments matching the criteria. Also test pagination by requesting multiple pages. Ensure the response contains only records as per the schema, and that irrelevant or out-of-schema fields are ignored. Verify that role-based access controls restrict access to authorized admins only. Edge cases should include empty result sets and invalid filter criteria.

Test that creating a thread fails when required fields (such as board_id, author_member_id, title) are missing. Omit each in turn and verify validation errors are returned.

Create author for the thread as a control case.

scenario.draft: Test updating the title and body of a thread. First, create a thread, then update it using PUT and verify changes are reflected and updated_at changes accordingly.

Thread author.
Create a thread to update.

dependencies.purpose: Board for thread.
Thread author.
Create thread to be soft-deleted/restored.

scenario.draft: Test updating a thread with a non-existent id. Attempt to update and expect a not found error response.
Test that updating a thread with invalid values (e.g., empty title or excessively long title/body, or values not allowed by schema) produces validation errors and does not update data.

Thread author.
Thread to be updated with invalid data.

scenario.draft: Test soft-deleting a thread by id. Create a thread, call DELETE on its id, and verify the thread's deleted_at is set (by subsequently fetching the thread and checking the deleted_at field).

dependencies.purpose: Board for thread creation.
Thread author.
Create a thread to soft-delete.

scenario.draft: Test soft-deleting a thread using a non-existent id. Call DELETE with an invalid UUID and verify that the system returns a not found error.

Test repeated soft-deletion of an already soft-deleted thread to ensure idempotency and error-handling is correct. Create and soft-delete a thread, then try soft-deleting it again and verify the outcome (e.g., no error or error indicating already deleted, per platform rules).

dependencies.purpose: Board for thread creation.
Thread author.
Create a thread.
Perform initial soft delete before attempting repeat deletion.

scenario.draft: Test listing post votes using valid filtering criteria, sorting, and pagination. A post and a member must exist with at least one vote cast by that member on the post. As a prerequisite, create a member, a post, and cast a vote. Query the list of votes using filters on post ID, member ID, vote type, and created_at (date range). Assert that the returned votes match the query criteria and that pagination metadata is present.

Create a post to have a valid post ID for associating votes and filtering.
Cast a vote by the created member on the created post, ensuring there's at least one record to query.

scenario.draft: Test listing post votes with filters that intentionally match no results. Use either a nonexistent post or member ID (ensure they do not exist) to filter. The response should be an empty result set with valid pagination metadata. This checks the search function's handling of absence of data.

Test successfully retrieving the details of a post vote by a valid existing ID. Create a member, a post, and have the member vote on the post. Then, retrieve the vote using the returned vote ID and assert that all expected vote details match the creation info.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member to be used for post voting.
Create a post to allow association to the vote.
Cast a post vote and obtain the vote ID to retrieve.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a post vote by an ID that does not exist. Use a UUID that is not associated with any post vote and verify the response is a 404 not found error.

Test casting a new vote for a post by a member with valid data. A member and a post must be created first. Attempt to cast a vote (vote_type among allowed 1,-1,0). Verify that the response returns the created vote and matches the input data (member, post, vote_type, created_at).

Create a post for voting.

Cast the first post vote to trigger uniqueness on the second vote.

scenario.draft: Test attempting to create a post vote with an invalid vote_type value (not 1, -1, or 0). Prepare a member and a post to serve as valid foreign keys, then attempt to vote with an out-of-range value. Expect a validation error for vote_type.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for voting.
Create a post to receive a vote.

scenario.draft: Test updating an existing post vote's vote_type (e.g., from upvote to downvote). Create a member, post, and initial vote. Use the update endpoint to change the vote_type, and assert that the update persists in the returned vote entity with other fields unchanged. Check vote uniqueness constraint still holds.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for post voting.
Create a post to be the subject of voting.
Cast an initial vote in order to update it.

scenario.draft: Test attempting to update a post vote with an ID that does not exist. Attempt the update using a made-up UUID and validate that the endpoint returns a not found error.

Test attempting to update a post vote with an invalid vote_type value. Create a valid vote, then attempt to update it to an invalid value (not 1, -1, or 0). Confirm a schema validation error is returned and the original value is unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for voting.
Create a post for voting.
Create an initial valid post vote to use for the update test.

scenario.draft: Test deleting an existing post vote by its ID. Prepare a member, post, and vote, then delete the vote. Subsequent lookups of the deleted vote should fail (404), confirming the hard delete.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for voting.
Create a post to receive votes.
Create a post vote record to be deleted.

scenario.draft: Test deleting a post vote with a non-existent ID. Attempt the delete with a made-up or random UUID, and verify the system returns an appropriate not found error.

Test listing public member profiles using pagination, filtering by display name, and sorting. Create several members and corresponding public profiles first. Issue a PATCH request supplying pagination parameters and a filter (e.g., display_name contains a substring) to verify that only relevant profiles appear in the returned paginated results. Validate that all returned fields match the schema. This scenario also tests that only public, non-sensitive profile fields are included and no authentication is required.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple member records to reference for profile creation.
Create member profiles associated with different members to populate the listing.

scenario.draft: Test the member profile list endpoint when there are no profiles in the system. Issue a PATCH request with default parameters and validate that the result set is empty and no error occurs. This verifies correct behavior for empty tables, such as at initial installation, and ensures a zero-result is handled gracefully.

Test filtering member profiles by location using the PATCH endpoint. First, create several member and member profile records with different locations. Then, request a paginated result where location matches a given city or keyword, and assert that only matching profiles are returned according to filter logic. Verify correct results for both matches and no matches, confirming filter accuracy and field matching rules.

dependencies.purpose: Set up test members to be linked with profiles.
Create profiles featuring distinct locations to enable filter-by-location testing.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving an existing member profile by its id. First, create a member and a profile. Then perform a GET with the created profile's id and verify the response contains correct public profile fields as defined by the schema, including id, member_id, display_name, and optional fields (bio, avatar_url, location, website_url). Ensure no sensitive information is included. Confirm successful retrieval and correct formatting for all fields.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member for whom the profile will be created.
Create a profile for the member to later fetch by id.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval failure when requesting a member profile by a non-existent or already-deleted id. Attempt a GET request with a random or deleted UUID and assert that the system returns an appropriate not found error (e.g., 404). Ensure no data is leaked and error structure aligns with system conventions.

Test successfully creating a member profile record for an existing member. First, create a member account. Then POST to /discussionboard/memberProfiles with required fields, such as member_id and display_name, plus optional fields like bio or avatar_url. Validate successful creation, correct population of all fields, and enforcement of uniqueness constraint (one profile per member). The returned profile must match all schema properties and be publicly accessible.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member record to link the new profile to.

scenario.draft: Test that creating a second profile for the same member fails with a proper uniqueness violation error. First, create a member and a profile (POST). Then, attempt to create another profile with the same member_id and confirm that the API rejects it with a uniqueness error without side effects. This ensures business rules—one profile per member—are respected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to use for duplicate profile test.
Create the first profile for the member to establish the conflict for the second creation attempt.

scenario.draft: Test creation failure when required fields (such as member_id or display_name) are omitted from the POST body. Attempt to create a member profile with missing members or display_name, and confirm the API returns a validation error explaining the missing or invalid input. No profiles should be created as a result.

Test successful update of an existing member profile by id. First, create a member and profile. Then, issue a PUT with new values for one or more updatable fields (e.g., display_name, bio, avatar_url, location, website_url). Confirm the response reflects the updated data, unchanged fields remain correct, and all properties adhere to schema. Verify business rules, such as only allowing updates to fields defined in the schema.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member as the basis for the profile.
Create a member profile to update.

scenario.draft: Test failure to update a member profile that does not exist. Attempt a PUT to the endpoint with a non-existent profile id and confirm that the system returns a not found error (404) with no side effects. This verifies correct handling of updates for profiles that are missing or already deleted.

Test failure when attempting to update a member profile with invalid field types or unsupported extra properties. Attempt a PUT with data that includes unexpected fields or invalid types for schema properties and assert the system rejects the update with validation errors. Confirm that the profile is not modified and database integrity is preserved.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member and profile, if required, to validate rejection of improper fields.

scenario.draft: Test successful hard deletion of a member profile by its id. First, create a member and a profile. This validates clean and irreversible removal.

scenario.draft: Test hard delete operation on a non-existent profile. Issue a DELETE request with a random or already-deleted id and verify that the server responds with an appropriate not found error, and no side effects occur.

scenario.draft: Verify that a moderator or admin can retrieve a paginated list of post snapshots filtered by a valid discussionboard_post_id. Then perform a PATCH request with a filter for that specific post ID and check that all related snapshots are returned in the response, that each matches the correct post_id, and pagination info is consistent with created rows.

Attempt to fetch a post snapshot with a correct id as an unauthorized user (not a moderator/admin). Confirm that the request is denied and an appropriate error (403 or 401) is returned.

Create the snapshot as preparation for fetching with unauthorized credentials.

scenario.draft: Verify that a moderator or admin can create a post snapshot using all required and permitted schema fields. Confirm that the snapshot is persisted with accurate title, body, editor_member_id, and taken_at timestamp, and that the response contains all expected schema fields.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a post snapshot with a discussionboard_post_id that does not exist. Confirm that the service returns an appropriate error due to foreign key violation, and that no snapshot is created.

Try to create a post snapshot omitting one or more required fields. Expect the endpoint to reject the payload with a validation error, indicating missing required schema fields such as discussionboard_post_id, title, or body.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a post snapshot using an id that does not exist. Expect a 404 Not Found error and verify that no data is changed in the system.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a post snapshot using an id that does not exist, and confirm the API returns an appropriate error (404 Not Found or similar).

scenario.draft: Test listing boards using filter and pagination parameters. First, create several boards with distinct values for categories, sections, names, and status (is_active, is_visible). Then, send a PATCH request providing specific search and filter fields (such as searching by section, category, code, or active/visibility status) and pagination controls. Validate that the response contains only boards matching the criteria, is paginated properly, and no extra or missing boards appear. Test with various filter combinations, empty results, and edge case page limits.

Test board creation with all required and optional valid fields. Supply proper references for category, section, and set fields like name, code, is_active, is_visible, etc. Confirm the board is created, returned data matches input and schema (including created_at/updated_at), and the board is retrievable via GET and appears in PATCH listing. Test that all business rules and valid parameter types result in successful creation.
Test creating a board while omitting a required field such as name, code, category, or section id. Expect a validation error indicating the missing field and ensure the board is NOT created.

Test creation of two boards with the same code or name (if uniqueness is enforced). First, create a board with a specific code/name; then attempt to create another with the same value. scenario.draft: Test updating an existing board with new valid data (e.g., change name, visibility, description). Validate timestamps are modified appropriately.

scenario.draft: Test updating a board using an id that does not exist. Attempt the update and confirm a not found/404 error is returned with no change to the boards data store.

Expect the new board creation to succeed if the constraint is released upon hard delete, or fail if legacy state persists.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board (capturing code value), delete that board, and then use code value in a subsequent creation operation to test uniqueness/constraint release on delete.

scenario.draft: Test attempting to delete a trending topic using a non-existent id. API must respond with a not found error, confirming no cascading effect or server error occurs.
